--- judge_0 (openai/gpt-oss-120b, JRS=-0.065) ---
The proof correctly states the target rate O(1/√T) (Dimension A). All assumptions are introduced before they are used, but there are several mis‑applications. Assumption 4 (bounded drift) is used in Step 5 only through a Cauchy–Schwarz bound, which is fine, but in Step 7 the proof treats the per‑iteration average \(\frac1K\sum_k\nabla f_k(w_{k}^{t,e})-\nabla f(w^t)\) as being bounded by the same \(\Delta\) that only controls the *average over e* (definition (3)). This is not justified and over‑estimates the bias term. Moreover, in Step 9 the quadratic term is bounded as if the bias were identical for every local step, leading to an extra factor \(E\) (the bound becomes \(4E^2\|\nabla f\|^2\) instead of the correct \(4E\|\nabla f\|^2\)). This propagates to later constants. In Step 12 the argument that the higher‑order terms \(2L\eta^2E^2\Delta^2\) and \(L\eta^2E^2\sigma^2/K\) can be “absorbed” into \(L\eta\Delta^2E\) and \(L\eta\sigma^2/K\) relies on the step‑size condition (Assumption 5) but the algebraic justification is missing; the condition \(\eta\le 1/(2L(E+1))\) does not directly guarantee the required inequalities. These gaps affect the rigor of the bound (Dimension C & D). The rest of the proof follows standard convex‑smooth analysis and the final rate statement matches the theorem statement, but because of the above logical and technical issues the proof is not fully sound. To make the proof acceptable, one should: (i) replace the uniform drift bound in Step 7 with a bound that holds for each local step (or introduce an additional assumption); (ii) correct the quadratic term handling in Step 9 by keeping the sum over e without pulling out an extra \(E\); (iii) provide a precise inequality showing how the step‑size condition controls the higher‑order terms in Step 12/16. After these fixes the proof would meet the required standards.
